correctness.rationale: An injective vertex filtration on C_n gives a nonconstant orientation sign word. A selected vertex-edge incidence forces both adjacent signs, producing a 3-color marked word with no adjacent opposite marks; any single-sign marked word must leave at least one edge with both endpoints unmarked. Conversely these conditions extend to an acyclic orientation and hence a filtration. The weighted cyclic compatibility matrix T(t) counts all allowed adjacency words, while U(t) counts each of the two disallowed monochromatic vertex covers; they are disjoint for n>=3. Eigenvalues at t=-1 yield the trigonometric Euler formula and least period 12. Independent integer-matrix evaluation yields F22(1)=263593441; exact evaluations for n=3..14 matched all twelve stated Euler residues. The formula is for faces and Euler only, not complete homology.

originality.rationale: The published full strong-cycle dihedral Euler-character theorem already establishes precisely the same three-symbol face criterion and writes the same general weighted transfer matrices T(t) and U(t) in the proof of its much stronger character statement. It obtains the identity trace at t=-1 as a special case. Consequently F_n(t)=tr T(t)^n-2tr U(t)^n is an immediate full-weight generating-function reading of its already-displayed combinatorial enumeration, and the Euler period and n=22 count require only substitutions. This is stronger substantive coverage despite the absence of the full polynomial in its title.
residual_risks: The dihedral publication does not promote the entire F_n(t) as a standalone displayed theorem, but explicitly provides the full weighted-language enumeration and both matrices, so implication does not depend on title.
